blocks.value: Type casting converts a value from one type to another (booleans can't be cast to numeric types). There are two kinds: widening and narrowing.
Widening (implicit): converting a lower-precision type to a higher-precision one. No data is lost, so Java does this automatically.

int x = 4;
double a = x; // a is 4.0
Allowed widening conversions: byte -> short/int/long/float/double, short -> int/long/float/double, char -> int/long/float/double, int -> long/float/double, long -> float/double, float -> double.
Narrowing (explicit): converting a higher-precision type to a lower-precision one. Data can be lost, so Java requires an explicit cast: (data_type_name) expression.

Allowed narrowing conversions: byte -> char, short -> byte/char, char -> byte/short, int -> byte/short/char, long -> byte/short/char/int, float -> byte/short/char/int/long, double -> byte/short/char/int/long/float. Casting a float or double to an integer type truncates the decimal — it doesn't round.
